title: Design System: Departamento Psicopedagógico — Colegio Lord Byron

heading.purpose: Badge card title only; same family as body, distinguished by weight/case/tracking, not typeface.

label.purpose: Copied institutional strings only: domain suffix, error detail.

shadows.name: badge-lift

shadows.name: grommet-inset
shadows.purpose: Small neutral inset shadow for the flat grommet ring hardware detail.

components.name: Badge Card
components.description: The login gate's single hero object: an institutional ID badge / access-terminal card holding crest, title, caption, perforation divider, primary action, and fine print.
components.html:
Departamento Psicopedagógico

Colegio Lord Byron

Acceso exclusivo para personal con cuenta institucional @byron.edu.pe.
components.css: .ds-badge-wrap { position: relative; width: 100%; max-width: 380px; } .ds-grommet { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 3px solid #e1e3ea; background: #f5f6fa; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); } .ds-badge-card { border-radius: 1.95rem; border: 1px solid #e1e3ea; background: oklch(0.99 0.006 100); padding: 40px 20px 32px; text-align: center; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.6), 0 2px 4px rgba(22,108,82,0.08), 0 24px 48px -16px rgba(22,108,82,0.28); } .ds-badge-title { margin-top: 16px; font-family: Poppins, ui-sans-serif, system-ui; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.125rem; letter-spacing: 0.025em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #166c52; } .ds-badge-caption { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 0.875rem; color: rgba(22,108,82,0.9); } .ds-perforation { margin-top: 24px; height: 4px; background-image: radial-gradient(circle, #e1e3ea 1px, transparent 1.3px); background-size: 8px 4px; background-repeat: repeat-x; background-position: center; } .ds-badge-fineprint { margin-top: 16px; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #5e6c72; } .ds-mono { font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; }

components.name: Primary Button (Holographic Sweep)
components.description: The gate's single verification action. Ornamented with a one-off skewed holographic sweep on hover — reserved for this action, not a general button pattern.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { position: relative; overflow: hidden; width: 100%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 1.05rem; border: 1px solid transparent; background: #166c52; color: #ffffff; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: rgba(22,108,82,0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #166c52; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(22,108,82,0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-sweep { position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 -33%; width: 33%; transform: skewX(-12deg); transition: transform 700ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1); background-image: linear-gradient(100deg, transparent, rgba(125,211,252,0.4), rgba(216,180,254,0.4), rgba(253,224,130,0.35), transparent); pointer-events: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover .ds-sweep { transform: skewX(-12deg) translateX(400%); }

components.name: Status Alert
components.description: Inline solid/soft status message, e.g. the login's auth-failure alert. Same solid/soft pairing convention used for warn icon wells elsewhere in the app.
components.html: No se pudo iniciar sesión. Intenta nuevamente.
components.css: .ds-alert-critical { border-radius: 0.6rem; background: #fce1e5; color: #c62e46; padding: 12px 16px; text-align: left; font-size: 0.875rem; }

components.name: Status Icon Well
components.description: Centered icon in a soft status color well, from the sin-acceso gate screen; corroborates the solid/soft status pattern as app-wide, not login-only.
components.css: .ds-icon-well { width: 48px; height: 48px; border-radius: 1.05rem; background: #fbeadb; color: #a8611c; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; margin: 0 auto; }

narrative.overview:
This system has two layers, and they should not be confused with each other. Underneath everything is a quiet, utilitarian app-wide token set — institutional green, cool near-white surfaces, a monday.com-style solid-fill status-color family — that predates this pass and already runs through the dashboards, forms, and the sin-acceso gate screen. On top of that, the login gate is the project's first surface built from an actual direction contract, and it commits to a single object metaphor: the page is not a marketing split-screen and not a bare button on a void, it is one physical thing — an institutional ID badge / access-terminal card, centered on a quiet secured backdrop, that a staff member already knows they're allowed to hold.

The badge world earns its materiality honestly. Where the build's own finish review caught an invented device — a chrome/metal gradient standing in for a badge grommet — it was corrected to a flat ring built only from --border and --background; where a "dashed divider" read as a literal CSS dashed border, it shipped instead as a true row of perforation dots. Nothing in this system should look photoreal or use a fake-material gradient to sell a physical object; flat tone-on-tone shapes carry the metaphor instead.
keyCharacteristics: One hero object per gate screen, not a hero-image-plus-form split.
Institutional green (--primary) as ink and accent, never as a large background fill.
Card-stock white (--badge-stock) reserved for the one surface meant to read as a held physical object; every other surface uses plain --card or --background.
Elevation on that one object is tinted with the primary hue, not neutral black.
Security/texture backdrops stay near-invisible (5% opacity) — texture, never pattern.
State color communicates via a solid/soft pair (--critical/--critical-soft, etc.) reused identically across the gate and the rest of the app.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Elevation on a "physical object" surface (the badge card) is tinted with --primary, not neutral black (rgba(22,108,82,…), not rgba(0,0,0,…)). Ordinary UI surfaces elsewhere do not carry this treatment.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: --primary is ink and action color, never a fill. If a screen needs a large green surface, that is a sidebar-scoped exception (--sidebar), not this rule.

rules.name: The Verbatim-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any string that is copied data rather than authored copy (a domain suffix, an error code, a technical detail) renders in Geist Mono. Authored sentences around it stay in Poppins.

rules.name: The Flat-Elsewhere Rule
rules.body: Outside the badge card, the system stays flat. Depth for ordinary state (warnings, pending states, errors) comes from the solid/soft color pair, not from a shadow.

dos: Do tint the badge card's shadow with --primary, not black — elevation on the one "physical" surface should read as belonging to the institution.
Do build perforation/ticket-edge effects as a dotted radial-gradient, never border-style: dashed.
Do render small hardware details (rings, grommets) as flat shapes using only --border/--background — never a fabricated chrome or bevel gradient standing in for a real material.
Do keep security/texture backdrops at ~5% opacity so they read as paper texture, not as a visible motif.
Do give a hero "object" component a larger radius (rounded-4xl) than the controls inside it (rounded-xl) — containers and controls should not share a radius tier.
Do reuse the solid/soft status color pair for any state communication (warn, critical, good, info, purple) rather than inventing a new state palette per screen.
donts: Don't fabricate a metal/glass/chrome gradient to represent a real-world material — the build's own finish review rejected exactly this on the grommet ring, and it shipped flat instead.

Don't apply the holographic hover-sweep to ordinary buttons app-wide. It is reserved for this one high-stakes verification action; putting it on every primary button would turn a signature moment into decoration.
Don't reuse --badge-stock as a general card background. It exists to make one surface read as held card stock; using it elsewhere erases that distinction.
Don't raise the security-hairline backdrop's opacity, or apply it to ordinary app screens (dashboards, forms) — it belongs to the gate's "secured terminal" story, not to the rest of the product.
